decisions.reason: Metering both rails does not change the defined power sources, diode OR-ing method, or source-selection behavior.
The source adds 5V current metering but does not change standalone USB activation, LDO capacity, or the loads powered from the standalone 3.3V rail.
Identifying LEDs as heavy 5V consumers does not change their 5V supply, switching control, or level-shifting requirements.
The rail-metering decision does not add, remove, or alter any connector in the current connector inventory.
Requiring current metering on both rails does not change the existing local-decoupling requirement.
Rail current monitoring is independent of panel controls, connector modes, and input GPIO mappings.
Although a possible second INA219 would use I2C, the source does not change the established SDA/SCL resistor value, placement, purpose, or population policy.
The proposed additional INA219 address is not a GPIO reassignment and leaves the current GPIO mapping unchanged.
Metering the existing 5V rail does not alter its enable GPIO, switching behavior, output rating, or powered-load set.
The current-metering change does not affect battery-charge indication, its LED chain, connector, or resistor configuration.
Monitoring both downstream rails does not change the battery connector, voltage range, pin functions, placement, or AXP2101 destination.
The source does not change the interboard connector architecture, carried power rails, signal pinout, or matching-numbering requirement.
